intuition: We need the node just before the one to remove. Use two pointers with a fixed gap between them. Move the front pointer first, then move both together. When the front pointer passes the end, the back pointer is in the right place to change one link.

Place a dummy before the head and separate two pointers by n+1 links. Once the leading pointer has passed the tail, the trailing pointer sits immediately before the nth node from the end. The fixed gap converts an unknown total length into a known relative distance.

The dummy makes removing the original head look exactly like any other deletion: change a predecessor’s next link. No values need changing, and the surviving nodes retain their order. Returning dummy.next also handles a list whose only node was removed.

steps: For head=[1,2,3,4,5] and n=2, attach dummy before node 1 and initialize fast=slow=dummy.
Advance fast n+1=3 links, so fast reaches node 3 while slow remains at dummy.
Move both once: fast reaches 4 and slow reaches 1. Their three-link separation is preserved.
Move again: fast reaches 5 and slow reaches 2. One final move takes fast to None and slow to 3.
Node 3 is the predecessor of node 4, which is second from the end. Change node 3.next from node 4 to node 5.
Return dummy.next, still node 1. Following its links yields [1,2,3,5].

codeNotes.note: A removable head now has a predecessor. The dummy’s arbitrary value is never part of the returned list.
The extra step positions slow before the deletion target when fast reaches None. A gap of n would stop on the target.
Bypass exactly one node. Both neighboring links already identify the retained prefix and suffix, so no additional reconstruction is needed.

keyDecision: Keep the pointers n + 1 links apart, starting from a dummy node before the head.

concept.question: Can two bookmarks locate a node counted from the far end?
intuition: A forward-only list gives no immediate position counted from its end. Counting the entire list first works, but a fixed gap between two bookmarks can reveal the desired predecessor in one coordinated walk.

Put a temporary starting node before the list. Move the front bookmark ahead by one more link than the requested end-distance. Then move both bookmarks together. When the front passes the end, the rear bookmark is just before the node to remove.
concept.observation: Keep a gap of one more link than the end-distance, measured from the temporary starting node.
approach: Place both bookmarks at a temporary node before the head.
Move the front bookmark ahead by the required gap, then move both together.
When the front passes the end, reconnect the rear node directly to the node after the one removed.
concept.correctness: The bookmarks start with a fixed separation and move the same distance, so that separation never changes. When the front has passed the end, the rear is exactly the needed distance before it: immediately before the target node. Bypassing that node preserves every other link and deletes exactly the requested node.

complexity.explanation: Each bookmark walks at most the list length. A temporary node and a few bookmarks use constant extra memory; the work is linear.

pitfalls: The gap must locate the predecessor.
Return the possibly changed first real node.
Count from the end, not from the beginning.
